findings.title: deleteMany retryCount clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` filter, so this SMS-only cron will delete *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1, including rows that were already successfully scheduled. Any future code path that increments retryCount for a non-SMS method will silently have its reminders purged by this endpoint. The branch should be combined with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: retryCount is never incremented when sendTo/message is missing, so reminders are retried forever
findings.body: The retryCount increment only happens inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block (else branch) or in the `catch`. When `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, which is one of the main failure modes this PR targets) or the rendered message is empty, the loop silently does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and will be re-processed on every cron run until the scheduled date passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 69 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is missing. These cases should also bump retryCount (or delete the reminder).

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount update can lose increments
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` computes the new value from the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (or the job is retried while a previous run is still processing), both read the same value and write the same result, losing an increment and allowing more retries than intended. Use Prisma's atomic update `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead. Same issue at line 195.

findings.title: Prisma update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unawaited-by-try: if it rejects (e.g. the reminder row was deleted concurrently → Prisma P2025 record-not-found), the rejection escapes the catch, aborts the remaining reminders in the loop and returns a 500 instead of the intended per-reminder error handling. Wrap it in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on no match).

findings.title: retryCount filter in deleteMany has no supporting index
findings.body: The new `retryCount` column is used in a `deleteMany` predicate (`retryCount > 1`) that runs on every cron invocation, but no index covers it and the existing indexes (`[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`) do not help because the predicate is an unscoped OR branch. On a large WorkflowReminder table this forces a sequential scan each run. Scoping the branch to method/scheduled (so an existing index can be used) or adding an index would avoid the repeated full-table scan.
